title: Locate inbound client message in the Marketing Model
item: One client email, call note, or ticket describing a marketing problem
questions: choice:section - which model location does the problem live in (being_feeling, searching, site_visiting, converting_sharing, outside_model, unclear); noul:spans_sections - do the symptoms plausibly sit in more than one section
action: Code stamps the section label on the ticket first, routes to the owning role queue, and when spans_sections is true attaches the ranked candidate sections for an LLM or AM to disambiguate
why_jev: Every client interaction starts with 'locate it first'; the section menu is closed and tiny, so one 150 ms call per message replaces an AM's habitual mental step and keeps the label from being stamped on an answer already written.
doctrine: Locate the problem in the Marketing Model first; location decides who works it and how urgent it is.

title: Place a client symptom at a funnel stage
item: A client's description of 'business is slow' or similar
questions: choice:stage - awareness, consideration, conversion, loyalty, advocacy, none_of_these; choice:evidence_kind - lost_visit, bounce_on_site, lead_not_closing, bad_review, unknown
action: Code maps stage to default investigation order (awareness symptoms trigger the visibility checks before any site-conversion check) and opens the matching checklist
why_jev: Clark's own example: 'no liposuction contact in three months' is almost always awareness, not loyalty. Stage is a fixed five-way menu with an escape, ideal for a cheap classifier reading free-form client phrasing.
doctrine: AM must instantly locate 'business is slow' in the funnel; zero new contacts points to awareness, not conversion or loyalty.

title: Classify an anonymous negative review's likely origin
item: One negative review with no matching patient record
questions: choice:origin - genuine_patient, competitor_or_fake, misdirected_other_business, non_patient_complaint, unknown; noul:contains_clinical_detail - does the text disclose treatment or health detail
action: Code routes fake or misdirected to the report-to-platform path, genuine to the PM plus senior-seo escalation queue, and any clinical detail straight to the HIPAA escalation queue
why_jev: The doctrine example is a reviewer who may not be a patient, which is an advocacy-stage question with a closed answer set; Jev gives a fast first triage so nothing waits for a human to open the review.
doctrine: A bad review from a possible non-patient is an advocacy problem; check fake, competitor, or misdirected first.

title: Gate client-requested page edits before publish
item: A client's proposed edit (diff) to a live service page
questions: choice:edit_type - cosmetic_wording, removes_or_renames_headings, removes_entities_or_terms, adds_new_claims, structural_rewrite; noul:touches_ranking_page - does the edit change copy that carries the page's primary topic
action: Code holds publish for anything except cosmetic_wording on a non-ranking page, then opens the SEO and semantic-signal analysis task and pastes the diff
why_jev: Months of body-of-document signal can be wiped by one well-meant rewrite; the AM script is 'pause publish'. A near-free classifier can read every diff the client submits so the pause is automatic, not remembered.
doctrine: Body-of-document signals built over months can be wiped by a client's rewrite; pause, analyse, then decide.

title: Tag page elements as primary or secondary conversion
item: One CTA or form element on a page, with its label and destination
questions: choice:conversion_type - primary_money_action, secondary_stepping_stone, navigation_or_other; noul:competes_with_primary - does this element visually or verbally compete with the primary action
action: Code counts primary actions per page, flags pages with zero or several, and lists competing secondary CTAs for the designer
why_jev: Primary versus secondary is a semantic distinction (booking a consult versus newsletter signup) that no regex catches, yet every campaign brief needs it, so it runs across every element on every page.
doctrine: Know which conversion makes money and which is a stepping stone in every brief so success is measured correctly.

title: Map page paragraphs to Being and Feeling questions
item: One paragraph from hero or intro copy
questions: choice:addresses - audience, core_desire, specific_problem, readiness_to_act, none; score:concreteness - generic (1) to a specific lived situation (5)
action: Code builds a per-page coverage table (which of A/B/C/D are never addressed, average concreteness) and flags pages missing two or more
why_jev: The four Section 1 questions are a fixed menu; a cheap per-paragraph pass finds the pages that never mention the prospect's actual situation, which an LLM would only do page by page at higher cost.
doctrine: Being and Feeling asks who the audience is, their core desire, their specific problem, and whether they are ready.

title: Flag practice-centred versus patient-centred copy
item: One sentence or heading from a service or home page
questions: choice:perspective - patient_perspective, practice_perspective, neutral_factual; noul:leads_with_credentials - is the sentence primarily the provider's CV or accolades
action: Code computes the hero block's perspective mix, flags heroes where practice_perspective dominates, and sends them to the copywriter queue
why_jev: Operating Principle 2 (write from the patient's view) is violated sentence by sentence; a perspective label is cheap enough to run on every sentence of every client page.
doctrine: Hero copy should address the patient's A/B/C/D, not the surgeon's CV.

title: Score core-desire specificity in persona statements
item: A persona or core-desire statement written by an AM or strategist
questions: score:specificity - generic demographic bracket (1), interest-level (2), named desire (3), desire plus situation (4), desire with concrete lived trigger and deadline (5)
action: Code blocks a strategy brief from advancing if any persona scores below 3 and returns the weakest statements for rewrite
why_jev: The doctrine's own bar is the 'cocktail dress and Christmas party' level of concreteness; an ordinal 1-5 gate is exactly what a score question does, and it can run on every persona in every brief.
doctrine: A core desire is a specific lived situation, not 'interested in cosmetic surgery'.

title: Estimate lead readiness stage from an inquiry
item: The first message or form text from a new lead
questions: score:readiness - just hearing about it (1) through actively comparing providers (3) to ready to book now (5); choice:awareness_stage - unaware, problem_aware, solution_aware, product_aware, most_aware
action: Code sorts the inbound queue so score 4-5 leads go to same-day callback and 1-2 leads go to a nurture sequence
why_jev: Readiness (question D) is a continuous judgment over short messy text; latency matters because a hot lead's first response is time-boxed to 15 minutes.
doctrine: Section 1 question D: frustrated enough to start searching, or just hearing a friend's story secondhand.

title: Judge whether a page block works for AI retrieval
item: One section or passage from a service page
questions: noul:stands_alone - could this passage be quoted as a complete answer without the surrounding page; noul:answers_a_question - does it directly answer a patient question
action: Code lists pages with fewer than N standalone passages and queues them for restructuring or a Key Takeaways block
why_jev: Section 3 now has two readers, a human and an AI agent; atomic retrievability is a yes/no judgment per passage, run across hundreds of passages cheaply.
doctrine: Site content must serve both the human prospect and the AI agent that may cite or summarise it.

title: Check trust-before-offer ordering above the fold
item: The text of the first screen of a landing page
questions: score:trust_first - leads with the offer or price (1) to establishes safety, credentials, and reassurance before the offer (5); noul:offer_before_trust - does an offer or CTA appear before any trust element
action: Code flags pages scoring 3 or less on medical, legal, and aesthetic clients and queues a design review
why_jev: The model's vertical-specific claim is that safety and trust must register before the procedure info; scoring that ordering is a semantic call over short text, repeated for every landing page.
doctrine: On landing the real conversation is safety and trust, not the specific procedure the prospect searched.

title: Classify a client's public activity for the interesting-client factor
item: One item from a client's public footprint (podcast, talk, interview, press, original article)
questions: choice:activity - speaking, podcast_or_interview, original_publication, community_event, press_mention, routine_social_post, none; noul:visible_in_last_12_months
action: Code tallies distinct active channels per client and writes the Client Visibility Investment value onto the account record used in quarterly reviews
why_jev: The doctrine says client willingness to be visible caps what the model can deliver, but nobody measures it; a cheap per-item label makes a number out of a footnote.
doctrine: A client unwilling to be visibly interesting handicaps the model; visible activity feeds user-interaction signals.

title: Detect weak handoff in intake response
item: A client intake team's reply to a new lead, as copied to agency
questions: noul:addresses_stated_problem - does the reply respond to what the lead actually asked; choice:next_step - consult_offered, info_only, deflected, no_reply_content
action: Code (with timestamps) flags leads where the reply took over 15 minutes or fails to offer a next step, and adds it to the monthly handoff-failure count
why_jev: The model's visibility gap sits at lead to consult; reply text can be read for a next step cheaply, giving agency a proxy measurement across the EMR boundary.
doctrine: Check that the lead handoff to the client's intake team is fast, with a 15-minute first-response target.

title: Pick the likeliest broken flywheel section from a monthly report
item: A month's report commentary plus metric deltas rendered as text
questions: choice:break_point - being_feeling, searching, site_visiting, converting_sharing, no_break; noul:evidence_sufficient - is there enough data to name a break
action: Code uses the choice only to order the AM's review queue and leaves the conclusion to the human
why_jev: The AM's job is finding the break in the flywheel; a probability ranking over four sections is a cheap triage input that prioritises which client reports get read first.
doctrine: When an engagement struggles, some part of the flywheel is broken; the AM's job is to find and fix it.

title: Route a client to the right vertical compliance profile
item: A client's practice description and service list
questions: choice:vertical - surgical_medical, nonsurgical_medical_or_medspa, legal, aesthetic_cosmetic_only, general_local, other; noul:health_claims_present
action: Code attaches the matching compliance ruleset (HIPAA, FTC, ABA 7.x) and review gates to every task for that client
why_jev: Nearly every SOP varies by vertical; a closed menu mapped by a catalog lookup lets code pick the rules once and apply them to every downstream task.
doctrine: Every SOP varies by vertical; compliance differs sharply between medical, legal, and cosmetic-only.

title: Classify page role to set issue severity
item: One URL with its title, H1, and nav position, attached to a crawl issue
questions: choice:page_role - money_service_page, support_page, utility_page, blog_or_news, archive_or_legacy, other; noul:primary_conversion_path - is it on the home, nav, or booking path
action: Code combines page_role with the hard fact (4xx, noindex, redirect loop, backlink count) to assign severity 1-4 from the matrix and an owner
why_jev: Severity depends on 'high-value page', a semantic call over URL and title; code supplies facts, Jev supplies role, and the matrix stays deterministic across thousands of crawl rows.
doctrine: Severity depends on whether the page is high-value: blocking a money page is critical, an archive page is low.

title: Filter polluting competitors from the top-10 SERP
item: One top-10 result URL with title and domain for a target keyword
questions: choice:result_type - genuine_competitor, directory_or_aggregator, encyclopedia, video_platform, forum_or_social, news, other
action: Code drops non-competitor rows before Cora or correlation analysis and flags SERPs where more than three results are polluted
why_jev: A polluted benchmark corrupts every later step, yet it is a simple type judgment per result; running it on every tracked keyword is trivial for a classifier and slow for a human.
doctrine: A polluted competitor set (directories, Wikipedia, YouTube) produces polluted recommendations; check the top 10 first.

title: Pick the redirect target for a broken URL
item: A 4xx URL with its old slug, any anchor text, and the catalog of live page titles
questions: choice:target - one entry per live page from the catalog, plus no_equivalent; noul:has_backlinks_or_traffic_history
action: Code issues a 301 to the chosen page when an equivalent exists and the URL has equity, and a 410 when no_equivalent, never a homepage catch-all
why_jev: This is a catalog-lookup: the question is which live page the old URL was about, and code applies the 301 versus 410 rule; far cheaper than an LLM reading 400 slugs.
doctrine: 301 to the most topically relevant live page; 410 for permanently gone; never redirect everything to the homepage.

title: Judge topical relevance of an internal link for pruning
item: One internal link with source page topic, anchor text, and target page topic
questions: noul:topically_related - is the target related to the source page's subject; choice:keep_decision - keep, nofollow_candidate, remove_candidate
action: Code removes candidates only in non-nav content areas, never in the navigation, and lists each removal in the Teamwork change log
why_jev: The initial link prune needs a topical-relevance verdict for thousands of links; deterministic counts find the hub pages, Jev supplies the one semantic judgment per link.
doctrine: Remove or nofollow unnecessary, topically unrelated links; keep links that support silo structure.

title: Check that H1 echoes but does not duplicate the title
item: A page's title tag and H1 text
questions: choice:relation - identical, echoes_with_variation, unrelated, missing_primary_keyword_in_one; noul:keyword_present_in_both
action: Code queues identical and unrelated pairs for rewriting under the Severity 1-2 versus Severity 3 split
why_jev: Exact duplicates are code-detectable but 'echoes without duplicating' and 'unrelated' are semantic; a pair classifier finishes a whole crawl in seconds.
doctrine: H1: one per page, echoes but does not duplicate the title tag.

title: Detect junk auto-generated image alt text
item: One image alt string with its filename and nearby heading
questions: choice:alt_quality - descriptive, filename_junk, keyword_stuffed, empty_or_generic; noul:needs_society_member_phrase - is this a society or board logo that should say 'member of'
action: Code writes a hand-correction task list for the media library, prioritising medical imagery and society logos
why_jev: Auto-fill from filenames yields strings like 'DSC_00435'; deciding junk versus descriptive across thousands of alts is the kind of cheap per-item check Jev is made for.
doctrine: Auto-generated alts from filenames can be junk; verify a sample and hand-correct, especially medical imagery.

title: Triage a referring domain for backlink risk
item: One referring domain with sample linking URL, anchor, and any contact details seen
questions: choice:domain_type - real_business, legitimate_directory, association_or_news, automated_spam_directory, pbn_or_scraper, adult_or_gambling, unknown; noul:has_real_world_identity
action: Code builds the disavow candidate list from spam, pbn, adult categories only, and excludes real_business and legitimate_directory by rule
why_jev: The doctrine's failure mode is disavowing real businesses and medical directories; a typed domain label plus a rule in code encodes 'worst in, borderline out' for hundreds of domains.
doctrine: Hesitate on domains with a real address and contact info; disavow only real risk, worst in, borderline out.

title: Classify backlink anchor text into distribution categories
item: One anchor string pointing at a money page
questions: choice:category - exact_match, partial_match, topical_lsi, generic, branded, naked_url, other
action: Code computes per-target distribution and compares it to the internal or external target bands, flagging over-concentrated pages
why_jev: Anchor classification is needed for every link to every money page, internal and external; the five-way menu is stable and cheap to run at crawl scale.
doctrine: Over-concentrated exact-match anchors signal manipulation; diversify across exact, partial, topical, generic, and branded.

title: Spot negative-SEO patterns in new links
item: A new link with domain, anchor, and page type
questions: noul:looks_like_injection - spammy gambling or adult anchors with no editorial context; noul:web2_property - unauthorised blogspot, tumblr, or medium page pointing at the client
action: Code counts flagged links per week and triggers the disavow SOP when two or more patterns recur over consecutive weeks
why_jev: Weekly spurts of low-value links are a recurring-work trigger; a per-link pattern call on each new Ahrefs row keeps monitoring continuous without LLM spend.
doctrine: Two or more negative-SEO patterns present means disavow is recurring work, not a one-shot.

title: Route a schema validation error to its owning SOP
item: One structured-data error message with the schema type involved
questions: choice:owner - schemalyze_owned_type, ymyl_person_physician_procedure, local_entity, unknown; noul:affects_rich_results_on_high_traffic_page
action: Code files a Teamwork task against the owning SOP and sets Severity 3, or Severity 2 if rich-result eligibility on a high-traffic page is affected
why_jev: Which SOP owns which schema type is a lookup, but error messages are free-form; Jev maps messy text to the closed owner menu and code applies the routing table.
doctrine: Flag schema errors and route by type: Schemalyze types to Schema Setup, Person/Physician/MedicalProcedure to YMYL tuning.

title: Decide whether an orphan page is worth keeping
item: An orphan URL with its title and first 200 words
questions: choice:disposition - add_internal_links, consolidate_into_other_page, remove_or_410, noindex_utility; noul:thin_or_duplicate
action: Code adds add_internal_links pages to the architecture map and sends the rest to the redirect map
why_jev: Orphan resolution needs a keep-or-merge judgment on content value; a short-text classifier handles the long tail of orphans so humans only review borderline ones.
doctrine: Orphan pages worth keeping need internal links; thin or duplicate ones go to consolidation or removal.

title: Detect keyword cannibalisation between two pages
item: Two pages' titles, H1s, and first paragraphs plus their shared ranking queries
questions: choice:overlap - distinct_intent, partial_overlap, duplicate_intent
action: Code flags duplicate_intent pairs when both rank for the same query and opens a merge or differentiate task
why_jev: Volatile rankings bouncing 5+ positions often mean cannibalisation; pairwise overlap is a three-way semantic call that scales to every page pair sharing a query.
doctrine: Rankings bouncing five-plus positions weekly often signal thin content or keyword cannibalisation.

title: Classify GSC not-indexed reasons by remedy
item: One URL with GSC not-indexed status text and its page role
questions: choice:remedy - fix_redirect_or_404, request_indexing, content_improvement_needed, intentional_noindex, wait_for_crawl, unknown
action: Code builds the prioritised fix list, limiting indexing requests to Severity 1 pages given the rate limit
why_jev: GSC statuses are many, wordy, and mixed with page value; a closed remedy menu turns a coverage export into a work list in one batch.
doctrine: Re-index requests are rate-limited, so prioritise Severity 1 URLs; bulk re-indexing goes through the sitemap.

title: Judge whether two NAP variants are the same business
item: Two listing records (name, address, suite, phone) that code could not normalise to an exact match
questions: choice:relation - same_entity_formatting_variant, same_entity_old_data, different_practitioner_same_address, different_business, cannot_tell
action: Code merges formatting variants into the cleanup list, sends different_practitioner and cannot_tell to senior-seo, and never touches different_business
why_jev: Code handles St versus Street; the remainder (practitioner-name variants, abandoned addresses) is a semantic same-entity call, and a wrong merge destroys reviews, so a fast first pass with a human on low confidence fits.
doctrine: Every character of NAP matters; mismatched variants create duplicates across 50+ directories and wrong merges destroy reviews.

title: Classify a possible duplicate GBP listing
item: A Maps listing found near a client's name and address
questions: choice:kind - active_duplicate, abandoned_old_address, practitioner_name_variant, auto_generated_entry, different_business; noul:has_reviews
action: Code files a flagged-list entry for senior-seo with screenshots and blocks any automated suppression action
why_jev: The SOP forbids acting on duplicates without review, but spotting candidates among Maps search results is a cheap semantic sort that makes the human's list short and correct.
doctrine: Do not merge or claim a duplicate without senior-seo review; an incorrect merge destroys reviews permanently.

title: Suggest the GBP primary category from services
item: A client's service list and specialty statement, plus the GBP category menu
questions: choice:primary_category - one entry per GBP category from the supplied menu, plus too_broad_or_unclear
action: Code shows the top three categories with probabilities to senior-seo as a proposal and records the decision in gbp-setup-notes
why_jev: Medical category taxonomy is a stated calibration gap; ranking a closed menu with probabilities speeds senior-seo's review without making the decision for them.
doctrine: Primary category equals the main service keyword, never a broad term like 'Health consultant'; senior-seo signs off.

title: Check a drafted review response for HIPAA safety
item: A drafted public reply to a medical-practice review
questions: noul:confirms_patient_relationship - does the reply imply the reviewer was a patient; noul:mentions_treatment_or_clinical_detail - does it reference a procedure, condition, date, or outcome
action: Code blocks posting if either is true, shows the offending sentence, and swaps in the approved generic template
why_jev: A warm 'glad we could treat you' is a violation even though no keyword gives it away; two atomic yes/no questions on every draft are a guard that is always on.
doctrine: Never confirm a patient relationship or reference treatment in a review response; keep it generic and local.

title: Detect PHI inside an incoming review
item: One incoming review's text
questions: noul:contains_phi_or_quasi_identifiers - does it disclose procedure names, dates, diagnoses, or identifying combinations; choice:response_path - generic_template_ok, escalate_before_responding, no_response_needed
action: Code routes escalate_before_responding to senior-seo plus the client's HIPAA contact and withholds any response until cleared
why_jev: The expensive error is responding to a PHI-containing review; a first-line classifier on every incoming review makes the escalation reliable and fast.
doctrine: If the reviewer's own text contains clinical detail, escalate before responding at all; when in doubt, do not respond.

title: Triage incoming reviews into response paths
item: One new review (text plus star rating)
questions: choice:type - positive, neutral, negative_valid_complaint, suspected_fake_or_competitor, spam, threat_or_harassment, contains_phi; score:urgency - routine (1) to same-day escalation (5)
action: Code sends type to the right template bank or owner queue and sets the response SLA from urgency
why_jev: Six response routes with different owners and SLAs; every review arrives in a BrightLocal alert, so a per-review label runs continuously with no LLM cost.
doctrine: Define separate response templates and escalation for positive, neutral, negative, PHI, and spam reviews.

title: Cluster review complaints into operations themes
item: One negative or neutral review sentence
questions: choice:theme - wait_time, billing_or_price, staff_attitude, communication_or_followup, outcome_dissatisfaction, facility, scheduling, other; noul:operations_not_marketing
action: Code counts themes per month and, when one theme recurs, writes an operations finding into the client report instead of an SEO action
why_jev: Recurring complaints are operations problems that SEO cannot fix; a cheap theme tag across hundreds of reviews surfaces the pattern that a one-off read would miss.
doctrine: Treat recurring review complaint themes as operations issues, not an SEO-only problem.

title: Screen review-ask scripts for gating and incentives
item: A review request script or message template
questions: noul:offers_incentive - discount, gift, entry, or priority for a review; noul:selective_ask - asks only satisfied customers or steers positive; noul:requests_star_rating - says positive or 5-star
action: Code rejects the script if any is true and returns the sentence that tripped it
why_jev: Small wording changes create policy risk; three yes/no checks on every template version replace a compliance reviewer's first read and catch drift when clients improvise.
doctrine: Ask neutrally; no incentives, no gating, never 'leave a 5-star review'.

title: Detect a review-gating branch in a client's flow
item: A written description of a client's post-visit survey or follow-up process
questions: noul:routes_by_satisfaction - does unhappy feedback go to a private form while happy responders get the public link; noul:sends_public_link_to_all - is the public review link offered to everyone eligible
action: Code flags routes_by_satisfaction=true as a stop and opens a PM task before the workflow is installed
why_jev: Review gating hides in process prose, not keywords; a yes/no on the described branch is the whole judgment and is cheap to run on every client onboarding doc.
doctrine: Do not route unhappy customers away from the public review link while sending happy ones to Google.

title: Check GBP posts for promotional-language risk
item: A drafted GBP post for a medical client
questions: noul:outcome_guarantee_or_superlative - guaranteed, best results, or similar; noul:before_after_language; noul:efficacy_claim_without_substantiation
action: Code holds the post for client approval with the flagged phrases highlighted; clean posts still require client approval for medical
why_jev: FTC and Google promotional-language limits apply to every post weekly; cheap atomic checks pre-screen the monthly 4-8 posts per client before human approval.
doctrine: Avoid best-results, guaranteed-outcomes, and before/after language in medical posts without a compliant disclaimer.

title: Flag patient-identifying content in photos before upload
item: Alt text, filename, and caption of a candidate GBP or site photo
questions: noul:likely_before_after_or_patient_photo; noul:contains_identifying_text - name, date, or chart visible per caption
action: Code stops the upload in the staging queue and requires senior-seo plus client attorney sign-off for flagged items
why_jev: Photo review is expensive and risky; a text-metadata pre-screen on every candidate (with a vision model only for flagged ones) keeps patient photos out of the default path.
doctrine: Before/after photos for medical clients are not uploaded without senior-seo and client sign-off.

title: Check that service pages keep primary geo mentions
item: The body text of a core service page after a content edit
questions: noul:mentions_primary_city_or_neighborhood - does the copy include the target place terms in natural context; score:geo_signal_strength - absent (1) to well integrated (5)
action: Code opens an escalation to senior-seo when a previously passing page drops below 3 after an edit
why_jev: A monthly retune step checks that edits did not strip geo references; a tiny classifier run after every edit makes it event-driven instead of monthly.
doctrine: Spot-check that core service pages still mention primary city and neighborhood terms after content edits.

title: Tier a citation directory by value
item: A directory domain returned by a citation audit tool
questions: choice:tier - tier1_core_platform, tier2_data_aggregator, tier3_vertical_specific, tier4_local_supplemental, low_value_or_spam; choice:vertical_fit - healthcare, legal, aesthetic, general, none
action: Code orders the tool's directory approvals so Tier 1 and 2 are done first, declines low_value, and compares to the vertical's Tier 3 list
why_jev: The doctrine says not to let tools default-pick directories; tiering a long audit list is a cheap catalog-style lookup that protects credits and prevents low-value listings.
doctrine: Prioritise Tier 1 and Tier 2 citations; a missing Tier 1 does more damage than fifty missing Tier 4 listings.

title: Screen directory descriptions for unsubstantiated efficacy claims
item: A short or long business description drafted for citation sites
questions: noul:quantified_or_absolute_efficacy_claim - e.g. permanently removes, clinically proven, outcome percentages; noul:contains_patient_identifying_content
action: Code blocks submission and routes to the vertical compliance reviewer with the flagged phrase
why_jev: Wrong claims propagate to 50+ directories and take 2-6 weeks per directory to fix; a cheap pre-submission screen is worth far more than the compute.
doctrine: Flag any clinical efficacy claim in directory descriptions to compliance before submission; citations are slow to reverse.

title: Check syndicated reviews for PHI before engaging
item: A review republished by a directory
questions: noul:original_review_contains_phi; noul:practice_response_would_add_phi_or_confirm_patient
action: Code routes true cases to HIPAA review and applies the no-confirmation response rule on that directory
why_jev: Syndicated reviews multiply surfaces where a response could confirm a patient; a continuous per-review check keeps the same guard across every directory.
doctrine: Apply the same no-PHI-confirmation discipline to republished reviews as to GBP reviews.

title: Propose the Area Served page subtype for human approval
item: A candidate area page: title, URL, intro text, and any address or map present
questions: choice:subtype - physical_office, geographic_service_area, symbolic_or_psychographic_region, unclear; noul:contains_office_data - address, hours, or office coordinates present
action: Code records the proposal, blocks content and schema generation until a human approves the subtype, and rejects any non-office page that carries office data
why_jev: The doctrine requires a human-approved subtype and forbids silently promoting a market into an office; Jev is only the proposer, and the escape option 'unclear' keeps it from guessing.
doctrine: Every Area Served page must be classified physical office, service area, or symbolic region before content or schema.

title: Detect subtype and schema mismatches on area pages
item: An area page's visible content summary plus its declared subtype
questions: noul:content_implies_office - copy implies a staffed office, directions, or hours; noul:implies_authoritative_boundary - presents an invented region as a formal jurisdiction
action: Code compares the answers with the approved subtype and raises a QA failure on any contradiction
why_jev: The failure to prevent is a phantom location entity; a pairwise check of content versus recorded subtype across dozens of area pages is a cheap QA sweep.
doctrine: Never place a business address, hours, or GBP on a non-office area entity; content, subtype, and schema must agree.

title: Detect secondary intent in branded searches
item: A search term that contains the client's brand name
questions: choice:intent - navigational, reviews_or_reputation, price_or_cost, customer_service, complaint_or_problem, competitor_comparison, other
action: Code keeps the term in the branded campaign and flags reputation, complaint, and price intents for PR or narrative-control work
why_jev: The easy-win doctrine says to watch brand searches for secondary intent; a per-query intent label turns the search-terms report into a reputation early-warning feed.
doctrine: Watch brand searches for secondary intent such as reviews, prices, or problems and respond with narrative control.

title: Classify search-term intent for waste analysis
item: One search term from a Google Ads search terms report
questions: choice:intent - navigational_to_self, research_or_comparison, transactional, competitor_brand, job_seeker, irrelevant_service, other
action: Code protects transactional, judges research on conversion data, treats navigational-to-self as likely waste, and queues competitor brands for owner review
why_jev: The SOP says classify by intent, not just cost; an address or suite number as a query is 'navigational to self' only in context, and thousands of terms make hand sorting slow.
doctrine: Classify zero-conversion candidates by intent: navigational-to-self is near-always waste, research is judged on conversion, transactional is protected.

title: Protect converting meaning before adding a negative
item: A candidate negative keyword and a short list of the account's converting terms
questions: noul:semantically_overlaps_converting_term - could this negative block meaning that has converted; choice:match_risk - safe_exact, risky_phrase, risky_broad
action: Code refuses to attach a negative flagged as overlapping unless a human overrides, and downgrades broad negatives to exact where possible
why_jev: Exact tests (did a term convert while a list was attached) are code; the fuzzy part, whether a phrase negative would catch near-synonyms of converters, is a semantic overlap Jev answers in milliseconds before every write.
doctrine: Before adding negatives, test them against converting search terms; broad negatives are the most aggressive.

title: Detect job-seeker and non-patient intent
item: A search term or ad-click query
questions: noul:job_seeker_or_employment_intent; noul:non_buyer_intent - student, DIY, free, or research with no buying purpose
action: Code adds exact negatives for confident cases and extends the starter employment list with new variants
why_jev: The 28-term employment list misses variants like 'plastic surgery assistant salary near me'; a per-term intent call catches long-tail job queries continuously.
doctrine: Load an employment filter list and build further negatives from real search-term data, not theory.

title: Spot location-before-service competitor terms
item: A search term that combines a place and a service
questions: choice:reading - reads_as_company_name_competitor, reads_as_genuine_demand, ambiguous; noul:is_competitor_brand_candidate
action: Code builds the location-competitor exact-negative list from confident competitor readings and holds ambiguous ones
why_jev: The doctrine's naming rule (location-before-service reads as a company) is semantic and applies to 1,400+ concatenations; a classifier does what a human cannot scan.
doctrine: Location-before-service reads as a company name and is negative; service-before-location reads as genuine demand.

title: Route a converting query to the best ad group
item: A search term with conversions plus the account's ad group catalog (name and theme)
questions: choice:ad_group - one entry per ad group from the catalog, plus new_ad_group_needed, plus none_fits
action: Code applies the Favourable Message-Match rule: adds the term as a keyword to the chosen group or creates a new group, and respects match-type rules
why_jev: This is a catalog-lookup: which existing ad group is this query about; thresholds (conversions, impressions, CTR) stay in code, so Jev does only the topic match.
doctrine: Add a converting query as a keyword when it improves message-match; otherwise leave it or create a new ad group.

title: Decide stick or twist for low-CTR converting queries
item: A converting query with low CTR, its current ad group, and the ad copy
questions: noul:ad_copy_matches_query - does the ad directly address this query; choice:action - reroute_to_better_group, add_exact_negative, keep
action: Code applies the filter thresholds, then executes the reroute or negative; keeps if the match is fine and the cause is elsewhere
why_jev: The filter finds low-CTR converters, but whether the ad speaks to the query is semantic; Jev supplies the match judgment cheaply per row.
doctrine: Low-CTR queries that convert should be rerouted to a better-fitting ad group or negated if there is no better home.

title: Spot landing-page mismatch behind high CTR zero conversions
item: A query with high CTR and no conversions, plus the landing page's heading and offer
questions: noul:page_offers_what_query_wants - does the landing page offer the thing the query asks for; choice:fix - change_landing_page, reroute_ad_group, add_exact_negative
action: Code lists high-CTR no-conversion queries, applies the fix choice, and opens a landing-page task for repeated mismatch
why_jev: The doctrine reads high CTR with no conversions as page mismatch; whether the page offers a variant the query wants is a short semantic check per query.
doctrine: High CTR with no conversion signals a landing-page mismatch; check page fit or negate if the variant is not offered.

title: Sweep ad assets for stale or non-compliant claims
item: One ad asset text (RSA line, sitelink, callout, snippet)
questions: choice:claim_type - accreditation, credential, trademark, superlative, drug_or_brand_name, price_or_offer, none; noul:needs_substantiation
action: Code resolves each hit through the asset-link enabled flag, then lists live assets with claims for compliance review and pause
why_jev: Partial-stem text search misses cased or rephrased claims; a per-asset claim-type label across every asset surface finds what a keyword sweep misses.
doctrine: Sweep ad copy across all asset surfaces for stale accreditations, credentials, superlatives, and drug names.

title: Gate Smart Bidding manual-lever recommendations
item: A drafted recommendation line from an audit plan
questions: choice:lever - bid_modifier, device_adjustment, ad_schedule_modifier, hard_exclusion, negative_keyword, budget_change, tracking_fix, other; noul:requires_manual_bidding
action: Code drops any requires_manual_bidding item on a Smart Bidding campaign and substitutes a note explaining why it was skipped
why_jev: The doctrine's confident-but-no-op error is manual levers on Smart Bidding; classifying each drafted action closes the loop mechanically after the bidding-strategy fact is read in code.
doctrine: Read the bidding strategy before recommending any manual lever; under Smart Bidding they are ignored or overridden.

title: Match a new finding to a recorded standing decision
item: A new audit finding and the client's standing-decision register
questions: choice:decision - one entry per register item, plus no_match; noul:contradicts_recorded_decision
action: Code suppresses re-litigated findings with a link to the dated decision record and surfaces only true contradictions
why_jev: Exempt campaigns top every zero-conversion sort and get re-argued each cycle; a catalog lookup against the decision register stops the repeat debate.
doctrine: Record counterintuitive calls with anti-relitigation notes so the next audit does not undo them.

title: Assign case-value tier to an ad group
item: An ad group's name, keywords, and landing page
questions: choice:service_tier - from the client's service catalog, plus unclear; score:case_value - low (1) to high (5)
action: Code applies per-service CPL ceilings and flags groups that pass the account ceiling but fail the service ceiling
why_jev: A single CPL ceiling hides unprofitable high-ticket services; mapping each ad group to a service tier is a catalog lookup that unlocks per-service economics.
doctrine: Do not trust a single CPL ceiling across services of different case value.

title: Classify call-tracking calls by lead quality
item: A call transcript or summary from call tracking
questions: choice:caller_type - new_prospect, existing_patient, vendor_or_sales, job_seeker, wrong_number_or_spam, other; noul:booking_intent
action: Code uploads only new_prospect with booking intent as conversions and suppresses the rest
why_jev: For medical clients call conversions dominate; unclassified calls inflate conversions and mislead Smart Bidding, so a continuous per-call label cleans the signal.
doctrine: Medical call conversions are load-bearing; measurement quality decides whether Smart Bidding optimises correctly.

title: Detect PHI in conversion events and URL parameters
item: A conversion event name, URL, or parameter string
questions: noul:contains_phi_or_quasi_identifiers - procedure, age, zip, or date patterns; choice:risk - none, directional_microconversion_ok, block
action: Code blocks the event from import into Ads or analytics and logs it for compliance
why_jev: Tracking that captures PHI is a HIPAA problem; per-event checks at tag-creation time are far cheaper than discovering a leak later.
doctrine: Conversion tracking that captures PHI is a HIPAA problem; use micro-conversions as directional signals only.

title: Check that ad keywords use problem language
item: A keyword or headline from a new campaign
questions: choice:language - problem_language_prospect_words, product_or_clinical_name, brand_name, mixed; noul:antonym_style_problem_focus
action: Code reports the share of problem-language keywords per ad group and flags groups below target for rewriting
why_jev: The easy-win audience brief says message in the prospect's problem language; labelling each keyword is cheap and exposes campaigns built from product names alone.
doctrine: Frame messaging in the prospect's problem language, not product names.

title: Pick a single optimised target URL for a DSA
item: A site page inventory with titles and H1s for one service
questions: choice:page_type - single_service_optimised, hub_or_category, homepage, thin_or_off_topic
action: Code selects only single_service_optimised pages as DSA targets and excludes the homepage
why_jev: DSA pointed at the homepage wastes spend; page-type labelling over a crawl list is a cheap closed menu.
doctrine: Point a Dynamic Search Ad at one specific well-optimised URL, not the homepage.

title: Check Smart Campaign themes are thematic
item: A proposed Smart Campaign keyword theme
questions: noul:thematic_not_literal_keyword; noul:matches_a_gbp_service
action: Code accepts up to ten valid themes and returns any literal keyword for rewriting
why_jev: Smart Campaign themes are topics, not exact keywords; a yes/no per proposed theme keeps builds compliant with platform expectations.
doctrine: Smart Campaigns use up to ten thematic keyword themes, not literal keywords.

title: Annotate metric shifts with a plausible assignable cause
item: A flagged signal from an XMR chart, the change-history log text for that window, and an external events note
questions: choice:cause - own_change, external_market_event, platform_or_algo_change, tracking_fault, none_apparent; noul:enough_evidence
action: Code lets only SPC-confirmed signals reach the annotation step, then stores the cause label for the Q1-Q4 quadrant decision
why_jev: Statistics decide whether a point is signal; only the attribution of cause is semantic, and the narrative-fallacy warning means Jev's 'none_apparent' escape must be honoured, never filled.
doctrine: Most day-to-day variation is noise; only act when a signal is real, and find the assignable cause first.

title: Check hero headline against landing-page checklist items
item: A landing page hero block (headline, subheadline, CTA, trust element)
questions: noul:benefit_led_headline; noul:cta_visible_and_action_oriented; noul:trust_signal_present_near_cta; noul:subheadline_supports_headline
action: Code scores the checklist per page, ranks the High-priority fails, and creates an LP fix list for the designer
why_jev: Many of the 93 checks are semantic yes/no judgments on short text; running them as atomic questions turns a manual spreadsheet audit into a batch over every campaign page.
doctrine: Hero needs a benefit-led headline, supporting subheadline, high-visibility CTA, and a visible trust signal.

title: Score ad-to-page message match
item: An ad headline set and the landing page's H1 and first paragraph
questions: score:message_match - unrelated (1) to same promise, same words, same offer (5); noul:ad_promise_present_above_fold
action: Code flags pairs scoring 3 or less for rewrite and holds scaling spend on those campaigns
why_jev: Scent audits are per ad-page pair; the same ordinal score on every pair makes mismatch visible across a whole account.
doctrine: Audit landing pages for message match with the ad that sends the traffic.

title: Classify competitor ad offers for test ideas
item: One competitor ad or landing-page claim captured from a transparency tool
questions: choice:offer_type - free_consult, financing, price_anchor, guarantee, credential_proof, urgency, other; noul:compliance_risky_for_medical
action: Code logs offers as test inputs and drops risky ones for medical and legal clients
why_jev: Competitor recon yields many ad texts; a typed offer label turns it into a test backlog with a built-in compliance filter.
doctrine: Use competitor ads for ideas, not gospel, and keep platform- and legally-sensitive tactics out for medical and legal.

title: Detect brand-name competitor bidding requests
item: A work-order line or campaign draft mentioning competitor terms
questions: noul:competitor_brand_bidding - does it bid on or name a competitor; noul:vertical_requires_owner_review
action: Code halts the task and asks the owner for per-engagement approval on medical, legal, and aesthetic clients
why_jev: The SOP carves out competitor bidding as owner-gated; a cheap detector on every draft ensures the carve-out is honoured even if a tactic arrives from a trusted source.
doctrine: Competitor-brand bidding is platform- and legally-sensitive; trusted source does not equal auto-approval.

title: Run Caples headline checklist points on each headline
item: One H1, ad headline, or primary CTA string
questions: noul:self_interest_or_news_lead; noul:has_specifics - numbers, dates, named procedures; noul:clever_pun_or_wordplay; noul:audience_specified_or_implied
action: Code tallies points per headline (ship at 6 of 7 with reading level from code) and ranks the 5+ variants by pass count
why_jev: Four of the seven points are semantic yes/no; running them atomically on every variant lets the copywriter iterate in seconds and combines with a code-computed grade level.
doctrine: Check headlines for self-interest or news, specifics, audience, and no cleverness; ship at six of seven points.

title: Pair-check hero and first 50 words against awareness stage
item: The hero block plus the first 50 words and a stated awareness-by-sophistication cell
questions: choice:copy_stage - unaware, problem_aware, solution_aware, product_aware, most_aware; noul:reads_as_one_continuous_promise
action: Code compares copy_stage to the brief's cell and fails the pair if more than one stage apart
why_jev: The brief names a cell; whether the copy actually speaks to it is a semantic stage call that the SOP asks for at sign-off but nobody does at scale.
doctrine: Hero and first 50 words are signed off as a pair and must match the awareness and sophistication cell.

title: Flag curse-of-knowledge jargon in page copy
item: One technical, clinical, or legal term in context
questions: choice:term_status - lay_known, needs_inline_gloss, needs_replacement, ok_in_context; noul:undefined_in_page
action: Code builds the first-read flag list, removes lay_known terms, and sends needs_gloss and needs_replacement to the copywriter
why_jev: The Heath check is a fresh reader flagging assumed terms; a classifier is a cheap first pass on every term, with the fresh-eyes human reserved for the ambiguous remainder.
doctrine: A fresh-eyes reader flags every assumed term and unexplained clinical, legal, or technical word.

title: Label hero claims as primary, supporting, or filler
item: One claim sentence from the hero or intro
questions: choice:role - primary_claim, supporting_proof, filler_generality; score:weight - minor (1) to the one claim the page lives on (5)
action: Code runs the strike-and-reread loop by removing lowest-weight claims until one primary remains, and prints the cut list for the AM to facilitate
why_jev: Aesthetic clients resist 'but we also do'; an ordinal weight per claim gives the AM an objective cut list instead of an opinion.
doctrine: Strike the lowest-weight claim and reread until one primary claim survives.

title: Check attribute-to-value chains in claims
item: One claim or benefit statement
questions: choice:level - feature_only, credential_only, benefit, customer_language_outcome; noul:chain_complete
action: Code flags claims stopping at feature or credential and returns them for rewrite to the full 3-link chain
why_jev: Dunford's chain is a stable four-level ladder; labelling each claim is a quick pass that finds credential-only copy such as 'board certified' with no benefit.
doctrine: Every claim must trace feature to benefit to customer-language value; stopping at credential is a rewrite.

title: Flag generalities and unsourced superlatives
item: A sentence from a page draft
questions: noul:unsourced_superlative_or_generality - best, leading, world-class; noul:replaceable_by_specific_evidence
action: Code lists flagged sentences with the generality highlighted and counts them against the page's allowance
why_jev: Superlatives are both Ogilvy-weak and a compliance risk in medical and legal copy; per-sentence detection beats a word list because 'the best' is not always a claim.
doctrine: Replace generalities and superlatives like 'best' and 'leading' with sourced specifics.

title: Judge snapper urgency as acceptable or manufactured
item: A deadline or scarcity sentence in a medical or aesthetic page
questions: choice:urgency_type - real_calendar_deadline, real_inventory_bound, manufactured_urgency, alarmist_health_claim, emotional_pressure, none
action: Code blocks manufactured_urgency, alarmist_health_claim, and emotional_pressure and requires evidence for the two acceptable kinds
why_jev: The SOP lists acceptable versus FTC-actionable snapper examples; a typed label with those anchors lets every closing line be screened on write.
doctrine: Only real calendar or inventory deadlines are acceptable urgency; alarmist or pressure language is FTC-actionable.

title: Detect quantified efficacy claims needing substantiation
item: A sentence from medical or aesthetic copy
questions: noul:quantified_efficacy_claim; choice:claim_type - outcome_percentage, permanence_claim, comparative_claim, safety_claim, none
action: Code files a substantiation request to the client for each flagged claim and removes unsubstantiated claims from the publish set
why_jev: FTC requires competent and reliable evidence on file; the repeated judgment is simply 'is this a checkable efficacy claim', which Jev can run on every sentence at publish time.
doctrine: Any quantified efficacy claim needs competent scientific evidence on file; remove or qualify unsupported claims.

title: Check legal copy against advertising and confidentiality rules
item: A sentence or block from a legal-vertical page
questions: noul:outcome_guarantee_or_specific_result; noul:superlative_without_basis; noul:identifies_matter_or_client_details
action: Code stops publish, routes to firm compliance, and requires written consent on file for any matter or client detail
why_jev: ABA 7.x and 1.6/1.9 apply independently; atomic checks run on every legal draft as a pre-screen so compliance reviews only what trips.
doctrine: Legal copy must avoid outcome guarantees and any case fact without written client consent; Rule 1.6/1.9 applies separately.

title: Pre-flag PHI and quasi-identifiers in content
item: Any text about to be pasted into an AI tool, tool field, or brief
questions: noul:contains_quasi_identifiers - age plus procedure plus zip or date combinations; noul:contains_named_patient_story
action: Code blocks the paste or routes the task to a BAA-covered surface or manual synthesis
why_jev: The HIPAA pre-flag applies to every tool interaction on medical clients; a guard in the pipeline asks the question on every payload before any non-BAA service sees it.
doctrine: Never paste patient-identifying content into tools; quasi-identifiers like age plus procedure plus zip can re-identify patients.

title: Decide whether a page is YMYL and which blocks fire
item: A page's topic, claims, and vertical
questions: noul:affects_health_finance_safety; choice:block_set - author_bio, medical_review, why_trust, key_takeaways, glossary, references, currency_stamps; score:claim_density - low (1) to high (5)
action: Code fires the always-on blocks for every YMYL page and conditionally fires references, glossary, and key takeaways from the thresholds
why_jev: Block-firing rules depend on 'does the page make specific efficacy claims' and 'how many technical terms'; these are cheap counts of semantic items across a page inventory.
doctrine: Author Bio, Why Trust, and currency stamps always fire; reviewer, references, glossary, and takeaways fire on content triggers.

title: Choose the verification path for each credential claim
item: One credential string (board, fellowship, membership, hospital affiliation)
questions: choice:path - instant_public_registry, needs_48h_registry_window, client_signed_disclaimer, unverifiable_remove; choice:registry_family - medical_board, state_bar, pubmed, hospital, society, other
action: Code opens the matching lookup or disclaimer task and blocks publish of any credential with no resolution line
why_jev: Which registry resolves which claim is a closed lookup; classifying free-form credential text routes the AM to the correct source and prevents unverified credentials from shipping.
doctrine: Never publish unverified credentialing on a YMYL page; every claim needs a registry check or a signed disclaimer.

title: Compare reviewer and author credential levels
item: Author and reviewer credential strings
questions: choice:relation - reviewer_exceeds_author, equal, reviewer_below_author, unclear
action: Code fails the block if the reviewer is below the author and asks for a better-qualified reviewer
why_jev: Credential strings vary in format (MD FACS versus DO versus RN); a relative-level call is semantic, and the SOP requires reviewer greater than or equal to author on every page.
doctrine: Reviewer credentials must equal or exceed author credentials, verified before the block is built.

title: Check that a prose claim can be expressed as schema
item: One claim in an author or physician bio plus the schema property list
questions: choice:schema_property - hasCredential, alumniOf, memberOf, medicalSpecialty, hospitalAffiliation, worksFor, none_representable
action: Code builds the schema-readiness sheet and flags none_representable claims as entity-consistency risks for strategist sign-off
why_jev: Mapping prose to schema properties is a catalog lookup that a classifier does quickly for every claim on every provider page.
doctrine: Anything in the prose that cannot be represented in schema is an entity-consistency risk; rephrase or accept with sign-off.

title: Grade reference quality against the source hierarchy
item: One citation with its source type and year
questions: choice:source_tier - peer_reviewed, recognised_health_org, secondary_review, commercial_or_vendor, blog_or_unknown; noul:older_than_five_years
action: Code rejects tier 4-5 and old sources unless justified and lists weak references for replacement
why_jev: A citation hierarchy applied to a reference list is a bulk typed judgment; it also catches lists compiled from a single search results page.
doctrine: Source hierarchy: peer-reviewed beats health org beats recent beats primary beats secondary; vet each reference independently.

title: Test key takeaway bullets for standalone retrievability
item: One Key Takeaways bullet
questions: noul:self_contained_passage; noul:plain_language_for_lay_reader
action: Code fails the block unless exactly five bullets all pass and returns weak bullets for rewriting
why_jev: Each bullet must be an atomic, retrievable answer; two yes/no checks per bullet run instantly when the copywriter edits.
doctrine: Five bolded-lead bullets, each a self-contained retrievable passage in lay language.

title: Mine reviews and DMs for voice-of-customer language
item: One sentence from a review, intake transcript, or DM
questions: choice:motive - appearance, confidence, fear_or_safety, convenience, social_proof, price_or_value, other; noul:usable_prospect_language - phrased as a prospect would say it, not clinical
action: Code groups sentences by motive and selects usable ones into the Conversation Brief after a PHI screen
why_jev: The brief requires 20+ reviews and transcripts mined for prospect language; a per-sentence motive label turns hundreds of reviews into a motive stack in one pass, then PHI is removed first by code or Jev.
doctrine: Mine 20+ reviews and intake transcripts for the conversation already going on in the prospect's head.

title: Tag page sections to buyer temperaments
item: One section of page copy
questions: choice:temperament_served - methodical_how, spontaneous_why, humanistic_who, competitive_what, none
action: Code shows which temperaments the page never serves and queues a supporting section for each gap
why_jev: Eisenberg's four temperaments are a fixed menu; a section-level label surfaces coverage gaps without an LLM reading every page.
doctrine: Pages must serve methodical, spontaneous, humanistic, and competitive buyers through proof, story, and comparison layers.

title: Screen intake text for Dunford weak-positioning answers
item: A strategist's one-line answer to each of the five weak-positioning screener questions
questions: choice:answer_strength - strong, weak, jargon_or_unclear for each answer; noul:prospects_understand_in_30_seconds
action: Code counts weak answers and makes positioning the lead deliverable when two or more are weak
why_jev: The SOP's two-or-more-weak rule is counting; classifying each free-text answer as weak is the only semantic part.
doctrine: Two or more weak positioning answers mean positioning is the lead deliverable.

title: Check divergence between client belief and data in a brief
item: A brief's client-believed binding constraint and data-suggested constraint paragraphs
questions: noul:constraints_diverge; choice:divergence_size - none, minor, major
action: Code requires the brief to state which constraint is being solved and why whenever divergence is major
why_jev: Trott's question 3 compares two free-text statements; a quick divergence flag keeps the brief honest without a full reasoning pass.
doctrine: Where the client's belief and the data diverge, the brief must say which is solved and why.

title: Test whether a blog topic trips the YMYL check
item: A proposed blog topic and keyword
questions: noul:medical_or_legal_advice; noul:names_a_practitioner; noul:makes_treatment_claims
action: Code routes any true answer to the YMYL SOP before drafting begins
why_jev: The YMYL trigger is run per topic before drafting, which is exactly three yes/no questions on a short string.
doctrine: Run the YMYL trigger check on every medical or legal topic before drafting.

title: Check that a blog supports rather than competes with its target page
item: The brief topic, target page title and H1, and keyword
questions: choice:relationship - supports_target, partially_overlaps, competes_with_target, unrelated
action: Code blocks competes_with_target and asks for a differentiated long-tail angle
why_jev: A post that cannibalises its service page is the costliest blog failure; a three-second check at brief time prevents it.
doctrine: Every blog supports a procedure page and never competes with it.

title: Classify planned internal-link anchors for blogs
item: A proposed anchor text for a post-to-target link
questions: choice:category - exact_match, partial_match, topical_lsi, generic, branded
action: Code compares to the Stage B anchor budget for the target and rejects 'click here' or over-concentrated exact anchors
why_jev: Anchor category is a five-way label; checking each proposed anchor against the distribution is trivial at write time.
doctrine: Choose partial-match or topical anchors for post-to-target links, never 'click here'.

title: Run the blog gate floor checks on a draft
item: A draft blog post section
questions: noul:contains_phi; noul:invented_or_unsourced_statistic; noul:absolute_outcome_claim; noul:unverified_fda_status_claim; noul:missing_required_disclosure
action: Code returns a clean-floor or fail result, reports the offending sentences, and still sends every draft to a human
why_jev: The gate is a floor, not clearance; five atomic checks per section are cheap and consistent, and a human still decides publication.
doctrine: Gate-pass means a clean floor, never legally cleared; every draft still gets human review.

title: Check internal link placement reads naturally
item: The sentence containing an inserted internal link and its anchor
questions: noul:contextually_justified - is the link topically relevant to the sentence; noul:disrupts_reading
action: Code removes links failing justification and re-queues them for placement elsewhere
why_jev: Links dropped by script into unrelated paragraphs waste equity; a relevance check per link gates auto-insertion tools.
doctrine: Every internal link needs context; a link from an unrelated post provides no topical signal.

title: Classify pages into link-architecture tiers
item: A URL with its title, H1, and rank-tracker keyword group
questions: choice:tier - money_page, support_page, utility_page, blog_page; choice:silo - one entry per service silo, plus none
action: Code builds the per-page link budget from tier and silo and the architecture map, then runs link-count checks
why_jev: Tier and silo assignment feeds every link budget; a catalog-style label per URL saves hours of manual classification on 100-page sites.
doctrine: Classify pages as money, support, utility, or blog and group them into silos before setting link budgets.

title: Judge cross-silo link justification
item: A proposed internal link crossing two silos, with both page topics
questions: noul:topically_justified_cross_silo - are the topics commonly combined or connected
action: Code allows deliberate limited cross-silo links and rejects the rest
why_jev: Random cross-linking fragments the topic signal; a yes/no relationship check over proposed links keeps silos clean.
doctrine: Cross-silo links are deliberate and limited, only when topically justified.

title: Check anchors for patient or case-identifying details
item: An internal link anchor on a medical or legal site
questions: noul:contains_patient_or_client_identifier; noul:case_outcome_specific
action: Code blocks the link and substitutes a generic procedure or practice-area anchor
why_jev: HIPAA and Rule 1.6 constraints on anchors are easy to miss on gallery and results pages; a per-anchor guard runs at insertion time.
doctrine: Never use patient names or case details as anchor text; generic procedure or practice-area anchors are safe.

title: Classify internal anchors in a crawl export
item: One internal link's anchor text and target page keyword
questions: choice:category - exact_match, partial_match, topical_lsi, generic, branded
action: Code produces the distribution report, flags over 30% exact-match and over 50% generic targets, and lists the specific anchors to change
why_jev: The Screaming Frog All Inlinks export has thousands of rows; labelling each against the target keyword is exactly cheap bulk sorting.
doctrine: Diversify internal anchors across exact, partial, topical, generic, and branded; flag over-concentration.

title: Judge Cora entity relevance to search intent
item: One Cora or On-Page.ai entity and the page's target keyword and intent
questions: choice:relevance - core_to_intent, supporting, tangential, irrelevant_noise; noul:natural_in_service_copy
action: Code builds the entity edit plan from core and supporting entities and drops noise before copy edits begin
why_jev: Entity stuffing is the canonical failure; relevance to intent gates every addition, and a per-entity label shrinks a 200-item list to the 20 that matter.
doctrine: Relevance to search intent gates every entity addition; add the high-impact missing ones first.

title: Decide whether a heading should be enriched or demoted
item: A heading with its tag level and neighbouring text
questions: choice:action - keep_and_enrich_with_topic_terms, demote_to_non_heading, remove, keep_as_is; noul:advances_topic_story
action: Code writes the tag-count targets and per-heading edit list into the cluster plan
why_jev: Heading zones determine the topic story; enrich-or-demote per tag is a semantic call repeated across every competitive page.
doctrine: Fix structure first: heading tags determine the topic story; enrich or demote per tag.

title: Detect off-topic drift sections on a page
item: One content section and the page's primary keyword
questions: choice:relevance - core, supporting, drift_off_topic; noul:better_on_its_own_page
action: Code computes a trim list (relocate or remove) and the density gain estimate
why_jev: Trimming raises density and focus together; labelling sections as drift is a short semantic pass that humans normally do by skimming.
doctrine: Trim drift: remove or relocate off-topic sections such as blog excerpts, comparison, and glossary blocks.

title: Check exact-match keyword placement in title, H1, body
item: Title, H1, and first 150 words with the target keyword
questions: noul:exact_in_title; noul:exact_in_h1; noul:natural_in_body_opening
action: Code adds missing placements to the action plan item list
why_jev: Cora's exact-match issue becomes a yes/no per element; code handles literal matches, Jev handles inflected or reordered matches and naturalness.
doctrine: Add exact-match keywords to title, H1, and body when missing.

title: Route ranking gaps to the right remediation SOP
item: A gap description from a Cora table, link intersect, or geo grid (one gap per call)
questions: choice:remedy - on_page_tuning, internal_linking, link_building, entity_optimization, schema, technical_seo, gbp_local, content_brief, image_optimization, competitive_moat, no_action
action: Code files the Teamwork task against the SOP owner, ordered by impact, effort, and dependency from code-held fields
why_jev: The doctrine says every gap must name a SOP; this is the cleanest catalog-lookup in the library, and a closed 11-way menu with escape is easy to calibrate.
doctrine: Every ranking gap must be routed to a specific remediation SOP and filed as a task.

title: Judge competitor referring domains as realistic link targets
item: A domain linking to competitors but not the client, with type and topic
questions: choice:type - local_news, association, vertical_directory, blog, university, vendor, spam; noul:relevant_for_the_client_vertical; score:attainability
action: Code adds relevant, attainable domains to the link-building target sheet
why_jev: Link intersect returns hundreds of domains; relevance and attainability are semantic and drive priority, while DR filters stay deterministic.
doctrine: Flag high-authority domains linking to multiple competitors but not the client; prioritise by relevance and effort.

title: Judge a content gap topic against the client's services
item: A topic competitors rank for that the client does not cover, plus the service catalog
questions: choice:service_match - one entry per client service, plus not_a_service; noul:buying_intent_not_just_info
action: Code files a content-brief task tied to the matched service and drops not_a_service topics
why_jev: Ahrefs content gap output includes irrelevant topics; a catalog lookup aligns each gap to a real service before any brief is written.
doctrine: Content gaps become briefs tied to client services, not generic topic ideas.

title: Classify GSC queries by intent and language
item: One GSC query with impressions and position
questions: choice:intent - local_transactional, procedure_research, symptom_or_problem, branded, navigational, competitor, junk; choice:language - patient_language, clinical_language
action: Code groups queries into rank-tracker keyword groups and surfaces patient-language problem queries missing a landing page
why_jev: Patient-perspective doctrine needs to know what language prospects use; intent and language labels over tens of thousands of queries cost almost nothing.
doctrine: Meet the prospect in their own search language, not the surgeon's clinical terms.

title: Match converting ad queries to pages for SEO validation
item: A converting PPC query and the site's page catalog
questions: choice:page - one entry per page from the catalog, plus no_page_exists
action: Code writes organic action items: no_page_exists means a new page, a match means tuning that page toward the query
why_jev: PPC data mining is a catalog lookup of query to page; converting queries without a page are the most valuable output.
doctrine: Mine a mature campaign's converting queries for organic page and site actions.

title: Assign pages and posts to topical clusters
item: A page or post title with summary and the cluster list
questions: choice:cluster - one entry per topical cluster, plus new_cluster_needed, plus none
action: Code updates the topical authority map and flags clusters lacking a hub or supporting posts
why_jev: Cluster assignment is a bulk label over hundreds of URLs and feeds both silo design and the content calendar.
doctrine: Supporting content builds topical relevance around a target page and funnels internal equity to it.

title: Judge whether an AI answer cites or mentions the client
item: An AI assistant answer and the client name plus aliases
questions: noul:client_mentioned; choice:position - recommended, listed_among_options, mentioned_negatively, absent; noul:citation_supports_the_claim
action: Code computes AI share of voice per prompt and flags negative mentions and unsupported citations for review
why_jev: AI visibility is a new Section 2 channel; mention and sentiment labelling across hundreds of prompts is exactly the bulk judgment Jev is cheap for.
doctrine: Visibility now has two answers: visible to the prospect, and visible to the AI agent mediating for them.

title: Track client tone trajectory from emails
item: One client email or message, with date
questions: choice:tone - warm, neutral, terse, cooling_pushback, abrasive_or_berating; noul:mentions_cancelling_or_scope_dispute
action: Code trends tone over 90 days per client and raises an at-risk flag when cooling or abrasive share rises two months in a row
why_jev: Tone trajectory is a named quarterly metric but nobody reads 90 days of email; a per-message label makes it a running series and routes the abrasive cases to the owner.
doctrine: Cooling tone, shorter emails, and terse language are early signs of trust erosion.

title: Separate urgent unplanned requests from planned work
item: One client request message or ticket title
questions: choice:request_type - planned_scoped_work, urgent_unplanned_request, scope_expansion, question_only; noul:must_have_by_tomorrow
action: Code computes the monthly must-have-by-tomorrow ratio and flags clients whose ratio is above threshold
why_jev: The ratio is a defined Anti-ICP signal; the only hard part is deciding if a message is a manufactured urgency, which is a semantic label on short text.
doctrine: Track the ratio of must-have-by-tomorrow requests to planned work as a manufactured-urgency indicator.

title: Classify time entries as inside or outside retainer scope
item: One time-log line with description and the client's scope list
questions: choice:scope - in_retainer_scope, scope_creep_related, out_of_scope_new_work, internal_admin; choice:sow_item - from the client's SOW items, plus none
action: Code sums scope-creep hours by client and computes effective hourly rate against the floor
why_jev: Scope-creep percentage requires line-item judgment against an SOW; a catalog lookup (which SOW item is this) turns free-text time logs into hygiene metrics.
doctrine: Scope-creep hours are those logged outside the retainer scope; track them with line-item descriptions.

title: Label engagement type for pricing fit
item: A client engagement summary (work mix, who delivers, how bespoke)
questions: choice:type - brains_frontier, grey_hair_experienced_judgment, procedure_repeatable; noul:pricing_matches_type
action: Code flags mismatches (brains priced as procedure, procedure staffed as brains) as renegotiation items
why_jev: Maister's three-way classification is a semantic call over a description; labelling every client each quarter makes margin leaks visible.
doctrine: A Brains engagement priced as Procedure is a margin leak; a Procedure engagement staffed as Brains is a quality risk.

title: Score ICP axes from evidence snippets
item: One piece of evidence (review sample, adopted recommendation log, communication note) tied to an ICP axis
questions: choice:axis - public_evidence_depth, advice_posture, geographic_profile, trust_and_civility; score:strength - weak (1) to strong (5)
action: Code aggregates per axis and flags any axis at 1-2, requiring evidence citations rather than vibes
why_jev: The scorecard needs cited evidence per axis; Jev pre-sorts snippets into axes and strength so the owner reviews a summary rather than raw logs.
doctrine: Score each client on four ICP axes with specific evidence cited, not vibes.

title: Check whether a recommendation was adopted by the client
item: A recommendation made by agency and the client's later reply or action note
questions: choice:outcome - adopted, partially_adopted, declined_with_reason, ignored, unclear
action: Code computes the 90-day adoption rate used for the advice-posture axis
why_jev: Advice posture needs an adoption rate, which means reading follow-ups; a typed outcome per recommendation makes it a number.
doctrine: Advice posture is recommendations made versus recommendations adopted over the last 90 days.

title: Detect Anti-Client hard disqualifier behaviour
item: One client message or call note
questions: noul:accuses_bad_faith_or_refuses_data; noul:berates_staff; noul:after_hours_intrusion; noul:manufactured_urgency
action: Code logs each true flag, and any flag in the quarter forces the case into the exit decision path with the owner
why_jev: These are named hard disqualifiers; a cheap always-on screen ensures nothing is missed between quarterly reviews, while the exit decision stays with the owner.
doctrine: Any hard disqualifier is an automatic escalation to the exit decision; the owner decides.

title: Score trust-equation dimensions from account notes
item: Account notes and client communications for one at-risk client
questions: score:credibility; score:reliability; score:intimacy; score:self_orientation - each 1 (low) to 5 (high)
action: Code computes trust equals credibility plus reliability plus intimacy divided by self-orientation and mandates a self-orientation remediation when above 3
why_jev: The diagnostic is a formula over four ordinal inputs; Jev supplies draft ordinal scores from notes, and code enforces the S greater than 3 rule.
doctrine: Trust equals credibility plus reliability plus intimacy over self-orientation; reducing self-orientation is usually the highest-leverage fix.

title: Spot self-orientation tells in AM client notes
item: A call summary or QBR draft written by an AM
questions: noul:name_drops_other_clients; noul:solution_before_listening; noul:refuses_to_admit_uncertainty; noul:methodology_talk_over_client_outcome
action: Code compiles a quarterly self-awareness report per AM for the 1:1 agenda
why_jev: The audit is meant for self-awareness, not punishment, so private cheap analysis of tells in notes supports reflection without surveillance feel.
doctrine: AM self-orientation tells include name-dropping, jumping to solutions, and refusing to admit uncertainty.

title: Detect patient-identifying detail in interview notes
item: Interview or call notes for a medical client
questions: noul:contains_patient_specific_detail; noul:redaction_needed
action: Code redacts or blocks storage of flagged lines before the notes are filed
why_jev: The hard stop is to never record patient-level details; a guard on every note before filing makes the stop automatic rather than a memory item.
doctrine: If a client volunteers patient-identifying information, pause and redact; do not record patient-level details.

title: Sort account files into purge, retain, or hand off on exit
item: A file name and short description from a legal client's account folder
questions: choice:disposition - purge_privileged_strategy, retain_aggregate_performance, retain_agency_internal, hand_off_client_asset, unclear
action: Code builds the destruction, retention, and handoff checklists and requires written confirmation for purge items
why_jev: The legal exit protocol has three buckets; a catalog-style label over hundreds of files prepares the checklists, with a human on every purge.
doctrine: On legal-client exit: purge privileged strategy, retain aggregate data under access controls, hand off client-owned assets.

title: Tag declined prospects with a decline reason
item: A prospect record and the decline note
questions: choice:reason - price_expectation, single_tactic_fixation, civility_floor, advice_resistant, wrong_geography_or_vertical, scope_mismatch, other
action: Code computes the quarterly decline ratio by reason and feeds it to the portfolio health review
why_jev: The decline ratio is a leading indicator of pricing power but needs a consistent reason tag; free-text notes become queryable with a closed label.
doctrine: Tag every declined prospect with a reason so the decline ratio is queryable quarter over quarter.

title: Sort health-interview answers by concern severity
item: One answer from a client health interview
questions: score:concern - none (1) to serious unflagged concern (5); choice:theme - trust, delivery, communication, value, scope, other
action: Code raises answers scoring 4+ to the owner and shares themes with the AM
why_jev: Interview notes are small but the signal is subtle; a scored read keeps ambiguous but serious items from being buried.
doctrine: The asking layer sits above the delivery layer; surface serious concerns the AM did not flag.

title: Judge whether a prospect can name their business problem
item: The prospect's answer to 'What business problem are you trying to solve?'
